result:
Nothing is built yet: the package prints a greeting and has two smoke tests. So this goes through the new-project path. The brief (`specs/ces-revisions-prompt.md`) has no numbered requirements, so I'm treating it as background rather than as a spec. That means every outcome below is a **candidate for you to confirm**, marked with where it came from.

I read the brief in full, but only the headings and opening sections of the three research files. Where their content shapes a candidate, I say so.

## Outcome candidates (unranked)

| # | Outcome | From | Cost (estimate; basis) |
|---|---|---|---|
| O1 | How the size of each of the four revisions (1st→2nd, 2nd→3rd, 3rd→benchmark, post-benchmark/wedge-back) has moved over time, for seasonally adjusted total nonfarm. Size means mean absolute revision, SD and tail quantiles. | prompt Part A/B; chatgpt §1.2 | Small: one ALFRED series (PAYEMS), a few MB, a handful of API calls under FRED's published 120 req/min limit. The real cost is your time checking how benchmark vintages line up. |
| O2 | The same history by NAICS supersector, seasonally adjusted and not seasonally adjusted (NSA). | prompt Part C | About 22+ series (around 11 supersectors × SA/NSA). I haven't checked how far back ALFRED's supersector vintages go; a probe could confirm. |
| O3 | Each seasonally adjusted one- and two-month revision split into a sample part (the NSA revision) and a seasonal-factor part. | prompt driver 1; chatgpt summary says no long-run published decomposition exists | Mostly arithmetic once the NSA vintages from O2 exist. The method is open, so only running it can measure the cost. |
| O4 | How the collection interval (days between the reference week and release, and the first-closing collection rate) relates to the size of the one-month revision. | prompt driver 2; chatgpt §2.2 | Collection days come from published BLS release dates (cheap). I haven't checked how far back first-closing rates go. |
| O5 | A hand-built annual series of BLS real appropriations, FTE and CES sample size, with shutdown, continuing-resolution and sequestration dates, set against revision size **descriptively only**. | prompt drivers 3–5 | Your time: about 45 fiscal years of budget justifications at a few figures each, roughly 2–4 days by hand (a guess from the page count, not measured). |
| O6 | A news-versus-noise split of each revision against a latent "true" employment path, for total nonfarm. | prompt Part C | MCMC time can't be estimated without a run. |
| O7 | Estimates, with uncertainty, of how much each driver scales revisions. The model uses stochastic volatility and Student-t errors, with shrinkage on the collinear capacity covariates. | prompt Part C | Can't be estimated without a run. |
| O8 | Benchmark error treated as an irregular, high-precision observation, plus how wedge-back spreads it across the intervening months. | prompt Part C; chatgpt summary | Can't be estimated without a run. |
| O9 | Driver effects by supersector, partially pooled across supersectors. | prompt Part C | Can't be estimated without a run; it scales with O2's series count. |

Qualities to place when the roadmap is written: manifests, traceability, full validation suites, scheduling.

## Proposed tracks

- **A: Revision-size measurement (O1, O2).** Known progression: total nonfarm first, then supersectors. Please correct me if you'd sequence it differently.
- **B: Seasonal versus sample split (O3).** Research. It answers *why* revisions move, and its answer stands without A's history or any model.
- **C: Collection interval (O4).** Research. Split from B and D because each answer stands without the others, even though all three explain revision size.
- **D: Institutional capacity (O5).** Research, descriptive. Kept separate so a hand-built covariate table doesn't wait on the state-space machinery.
- **E: Joint multi-vintage model (O6–O9).** Research. Split from B–D because their descriptive answers would otherwise wait on MCMC. E would draw on their data rather than block them.

The brief bundles all of this into one design. Splitting it is my proposal. If you'd rather fold B–D into E, say so.

## Choices already made

- Python 3.14, uv, pytest and ruff (repo).
- NumPyro (NUTS), Dynamax, Blackjax only if a custom kernel is needed, ArviZ and Polars (prompt, Part C).
- Units are thousands of jobs (prompt).

**Proposed name:** `ces-revision-scale`, giving `specs/ces-revision-scale-roadmap.md`. No roadmap file exists in `specs/` now.

**Optional probe (only if you say yes):** fetch the full ALFRED vintage history for PAYEMS and one supersector series. That would firm up the O1/O2 cost and show how far back supersector vintages go.

---

**One request:** please rank the outcomes within each track and the tracks among themselves. Also confirm or change the outcomes, the tracks, their kinds and the name, and tell me whether to run the probe.
